description: MIRAGE develops a tool that transforms RTL code to protect hardware designs from AI-assisted reverse engineering.
funding_summary: The project received a €150,000 Proof-of-Concept Grant from the European Research Council (ERC).
inflection_why_now: With the rise of AI models capable of reverse-engineering hardware designs, securing intellectual property in chip development is increasingly critical.
devils_advocate_risks: Technical Complexity: Ensuring the transformed RTL code maintains functionality while being unrecognizable to AI systems is technically challenging.
Industry Adoption: Convincing hardware companies to adopt new security measures may face resistance due to established workflows.

lp_synergy_matches.reason: Evonik specializes in advanced materials and chemicals, aligning with MIRAGE's focus on hardware design security.
SAP's expertise in enterprise software solutions could complement MIRAGE's technology in secure hardware design sharing.
